A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same APG research work, with readable main text, equations, Tables 1–10, Figures 1–23, and Appendices A–E. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix C, plus the Gaussian-mixture simulation in Figure 13.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and simulation results, including the APG–CFG comparisons, ablations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: APG retains the same projection, rescaling, reverse momentum, and denoised-prediction conversions. Algorithm 1 only renames normalized_guidance to adaptive_projected_guidance; its operations and defaults are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet class-conditional generation, MS COCO 2017 text-to-image evaluation, text-rendering examples, and the same synthetic Gaussian-mixture task. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: CFG in the principal experiments, CFG Rescale in Figure 11, and the same CADS, interval guidance, ICG, and TSG comparisons in Appendix C.

E3.justification: The pretrained models, samplers, metrics, guidance settings, and Table 10 hyperparameters are unchanged. Appendix D retains the 10,000-generated-image ImageNet evaluation and MS COCO 2017 evaluation subset.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Tables 2 and 9, prediction-type comparison in Figure 12, guidance and sampling-step sweeps, Gaussian-mixture analysis, and condition-alignment analysis are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate and KDE reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted curves, and qualitative image examples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains EDM2-S FID values of 10.42 for CFG and 6.49 for APG at guidance scale 4.

T1.justification: Before Equation (5), v2 explicitly assumes that the denoised prediction and parallel guidance component have the same direction. This supplies a necessary condition for the norm-ratio gain identity that v1 presented without qualification. Other equations and appendix derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about reducing oversaturation, improving FID and recall, preserving precision, and adding negligible computational overhead.

C2.justification: The same-direction assumption newly qualifies Section 4's explanation that the parallel component acts as a saturation-increasing gain. Other interpretations and the Section 6 limitation concerning two denoiser queries per sampling step remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation instructions, hyperparameters, evaluation details, hardware timings, and code-access information are unchanged. The Algorithm 1 function rename adds no technical information and changes no implementation behavior.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography are unchanged, including positioning relative to diversity-enhancing guidance, dynamic thresholding, CFG Rescale, and earlier projection-based approaches.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to the Equation (5) qualification, the Algorithm 1 function name, and publication/version text. Section organization and the remaining prose are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ICLR 2025 publication header and updates the arXiv margin stamp. Figures, tables, captions, and their page placements remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes explicit the directional assumption needed for Equation (5), improving the mathematical precision and scope of the saturation explanation. This is a limited correction; the method, empirical evidence, and remaining discussion are unchanged.
